summary.headline: Apollo Pipes targets INR400 crore Q1 FY27 revenue and 35% revenue CAGR to INR5,000 crore by FY31 after FY26 consol EBITDA fell 30%.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as volatile: PVC fell 15% in the first 8 months, rallied 75% over the next 4, then fell 25% in 2 months to about INR84/kg. Standalone volume rose 7% and Kisan was flat; the company crossed 1 lakh tonnes of annual sales volume and consolidated EBITDA fell 30% on inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and fixed costs of new verticals. Q4 revenue was about INR350 crore at NSR of about INR110/kg, and management guided to INR400 crore for Q1 FY27 with double-digit volume growth. Management expects Kisan to be merged into Apollo Pipes later, and South India plant to go live around FY28 end.

financial_highlights.value: up 7% YoY; crossed 1 lakh tonne annual volume

financial_highlights.change: vs INR60 crore in Q3 (volume 5,000 tonne)

segments.name: Apollo Pipes standalone (PVC pipes)
segments.commentary: Target EBITDA of INR8,000-10,000/tonne (about 10% margin), with spreads expected to rise from INR8,000 to INR8,500-9,000/tonne. Plumbing construction is about 60-65% of sales; agri and government infra about 35-40%.

segments.name: Kisan Mouldings
segments.commentary: Currently barely breakeven, with EBITDA of about -1% to -2% over the last 4 quarters. Targets INR5,000-6,000/tonne sustainable EBITDA, with a plan to scale to INR500 crore, then INR1,000 crore revenue at 10-12% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Window profiles and allied products
segments.commentary: Contributes about 1.5% of total sales, sold per length rather than per kg; present in North and South India. Expected to contribute at least 4-5% of construction plumbing revenue this year.

segments.name: CPVC and water tanks
segments.commentary: CPVC grew about 10% in FY26 and is expected to grow more than 20% in FY27 with Lubrizol tie-up support; water tanks grew 20-30%.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 revenue target of INR400 crore or more, about 15% QoQ and 40-45% YoY growth per analyst framing, with double-digit volume growth.
5-year plan: 35% revenue CAGR to INR5,000 crore by FY31; industry assumed to grow 7-8%, with market share rising from about 2-2.5% to 3-3.5% in 3-4 years.
Standalone EBITDA target INR8,000-10,000/tonne (about 10% margin); consolidated EBITDA per tonne expected to move from INR6,000-8,000 toward INR10,000-12,000 over 2-3 years.
FY27 capex about INR100 crore, covering Kisan capacity and brownfield expansion at existing plants.
Inventory days expected to fall 5-10 days in FY27; working capital cycle targeted below 35 days in FY27 (internal target 30 days by March 2027).
Kisan to be merged into Apollo Pipes Limited; timeline to be shared in coming investor calls.
capex_capacity: Three plants at about INR1,000 crore revenue potential each: North India (main), West India, and Varanasi (now fully operational).
New South India plant (Malur/Tumkur/Bangalore belt): land work to start after about a year; go-live about 18 months after land finalisation, expected around FY28 end.
Kisan plant can reach about INR500 crore revenue with INR30-40 crore capex already incurred; a further INR50-60 crore brownfield expansion targets INR1,000 crore.
Current installed capacity cited as INR3,000 crore revenue potential, against INR1,100 crore FY26 revenue.
demand_pricing: Demand described as encouraging; April was good but below expectations after a strong March channel fill. Agri demand is good and rural is outperforming urban over the last 2-3 months.
Channel inventory is low to normal after destocking; channel refilling from May and June, a seasonal quarter.

PVC resin: Reliance around INR84-85/kg vs local trade about INR79/kg. Management expects a move of plus/minus 5% in the near term; the duty exemption ends 30 June, after which 8.25% duty applies and may push prices up.
Expected import surge for 15-30 days before duty returns; management expects monsoon demand pressure in Q2.
Gross margin fell YoY and QoQ despite 13-14% higher realisation, due to aggressive pricing, window profile sampling costs and write-downs on unsold finished goods; inventory gains were negligible.
Competition has intensified over 3-4 years with price war among organised players; management expects capacity clean-up of small unorganised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall despite higher realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited aggressive pricing to rebuild volume, window profile sampling costs, and write-downs from clearing unsold finished-goods inventory. Raw material inventory gains were negligible.

qa_highlights.question: Is April volume on track for the INR400 crore Q1 target after destocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track, with channel inventory already low and refilling from May; April was light after a heavy March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kisan performance disappoint in Q4 and what happens next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jan-Feb demand was weak, so push sales hurt margins; Q4 revenue rose to INR80 crore with volume up to about 7,000 tonne, and margins should improve from Q1 with operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and when will the South India plant come?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR100 crore. The South plant is expected around FY28 end, about 18 months after land is finalised, with work starting after roughly a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Cycle rose to 45-46 days from 35 in FY25, mainly from inventory days (80 vs 70). Management expects below 35 days in FY27, with an internal target of 30 days by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach 35% CAGR and what is the market share outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current share is about 2-2.5% of a about INR55,000 crore market; management targets 3-3.5% in 3-4 years, assuming 7-8% industry growth, taking share from smaller unorganised players.

risks_watch: PVC price volatility and crude-linked import dynamics ahead of duty change on 1 July; possible import surge followed by Q2 monsoon demand pressure.
Gross margin compression from continued aggressive pricing; whether standalone EBITDA holds INR8,000-10,000/tonne as volume rises.
Kisan Mouldings near-breakeven margins and its planned merger into Apollo Pipes; merger terms and timeline pending.
Working capital cycle elevated at 45-46 days; watch inventory days trend toward 30-35 days.
Government infrastructure demand still weak; Ashirvad promoter's planned large pipe plant in FY27 could intensify competition.
Warrant expiry this year, with the South India plant not yet in the FY27 capex plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on volume and the 35% CAGR plan, but evasive on PVC price direction and April volumes, saying outcomes are uncertain. Management acknowledged margin pressure and Kisan underperformance without giving a firm quantified margin recovery timeline.

growth.why: Management targets INR400 crore+ revenue in Q1 FY27 and a 35% revenue CAGR to INR5,000 crore by FY31, but the brief gives no specific new capacity for the near term: the South India plant is about 7 quarters out, Kisan expansion is INR50-60 crore, and the plants are described as highly underutilised, so backing is partial.
